newsitem.title: GREECE: First tranche set for Greek Elefsinas highway.
newsitem.headline: First tranche set for Greek Elefsinas highway.

text.p: Greece and the European Investment Bank (EIB) will sign a loan agreement on December 16 worth 45 billion drachmas ($184.6 million), the first tranche of a loan for building the Elefsina-Stavros highway, the EIB said in a statement.
The agreement will be signed by National Economy Minister Yannos Papantoniou and the EIB's vice-president, it said.

Parliament passed a bill recently on terms for construction and financing of the project. The highway will connect the Elefsina, Stavros, Spata and Ymittos areas of Attica. Construction is expected to begin on May 30, 1997, when financing procedures will be completed.
The contractual period of the project will be five years. Construction will coincide with the building of the new Athens airport at Spata.

The concession group responsible for financing, construction and maintenance of the highway comprises 14 Greek companies and the French company Transroute. Leader is Greek construction company, Aktor.

The project will be operated under a Build Operate Transfer (BOT) system. This means that the concession company will be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the highway and will turn it over to the state after 18 years.
The project is self-financed, at an estimated cost of 235 billion drachmas, in late May 1994 prices.
